citation: docs/architecture.md, ownership of truth: Muster names its own tabs. docs/cli/overview.md, tab names. kan a_29e9boMfk.
why: Muster names its own tabs, and the daemon knows each tab by that name: it goes into the request that makes the tab. A tab is named so that a script, a CLI or an agent can address it, and a tab spanning two machines is one name held on both daemons. These cases pin the spelling a mint produces at an instant and a seed, since a name is a contract with whatever has read one. The properties no single spelling can state - that a drawn name is never handed out twice, and that later names sort after earlier ones - are asserted natively in the driver.

cases.name: a name says when its tab was made
cases.why: Two tabs made ten seconds apart get names that sort into the order they were made. Pinned rather than assumed, because it falls out of the epoch and the tick size being chosen together and a change to either would lose it silently.

cases.name: a tab minted later in the day sorts after one minted earlier
cases.why: The same property, stated as the comparison somebody actually depends on. A later instant has to spell a name that sorts after an earlier one, which is what stops a list of tab names read off two runs coming back in the wrong order.
